title: Origins of the Murle
subtitle: Tracing the roots of a resilient people
body: The Murle are a Nilotic people whose story stretches back many generations across the plains and river valleys of what is now South Sudan. Oral tradition, passed carefully from elder to child, remains one of the richest sources for understanding where the community began and how it grew.

Elders describe early ancestors as cattle-keeping communities who moved with the seasons, following rains and pasture. This mobile way of life shaped much of Murle identity: a deep relationship with cattle, an intimate knowledge of the land, and social structures built to organize movement, defense, and cooperation.

Place names, clan histories, and songs preserve fragments of this early period. While written records from outside the community are sparse, the consistency of oral accounts across different clans offers a shared narrative thread that modern historians and cultural custodians continue to document.
This app exists to gather these fragments in one place — not as a final word, but as a starting point for deeper conversations between generations.
